    Section

    Free agents, skills and workflows

    Everything here is free to install. Each item says how well it has been tested, and none of the labels are rounded up.

    Free to install·labels from recorded test runs

    37 free items · 6 workflows · 52 individual skills, agents and hooks inside the Foundry plugins

    Add the AI Foundry marketplace once

    claude plugin marketplace add ai-foundry-byu/foundry-marketplace

    Then install any Foundry plugin by name, or type /plugin inside Claude Code to browse. The Foundry's own item pages are at its marketplace site.

    What the labels mean
    • verified Passed a live end-to-end run of its main path in a real Claude Code session.
    • beta Partly live-tested or unit-tested, with known gaps.
    • new Little or no live testing yet. Try it on something low stakes first.
    • unrated Not part of the Foundry's recorded test runs. Its README states its own limits.

    Plugins

    Install a whole set in one command. Updates come with it.

    1. betaStarter set · AI FoundryMIT

      foundry-sdlc

      The 8-stage 0-to-1 workflow: scaffold, requirements, PRD and stories, workplan, parallel lanes, QA, ship, feedback. Templates, a PRD-to-stories compiler, a stage detector, and two independent judge agents (prd-critic, story-verifier).

      Labeled by its weakest item. 10 verified, 1 beta.

      Terminal

      claude plugin marketplace add ai-foundry-byu/foundry-marketplace && claude plugin install foundry-sdlc@ai-foundry
      Known limits
      • Projects scaffolded before this release keep an old tools/gen_stories.py; run gen_stories.py --refresh-tools if the stage readout sticks at 4.
      • Parallel lanes are protected only as subagents with worktree isolation.
      • On smaller models, call a skill by name. Triggering is tuned for Sonnet and Opus.
      What is inside: 2 agents, 1 hook, 8 skills
      • prd-criticagentverified
      • story-verifieragentverified
      • sdlc-stagehookverified
      • bug-to-storyskillverified
      • gather-requirementsskillverified
      • new-projectskillverified
      • parallel-lanesskillverified
      • sdlcskillverified
      • shipskillbeta
      • write-prdskillverified
      • write-workplanskillverified

      Source · Item pages

    2. betaStarter set · AI FoundryMIT

      foundry-guardrails

      Hooks that make the gates real: block destructive commands and secret leaks, require tests before done and before push or deploy, keep worktree sessions in their worktree, flag stale whole-file writes, and keep working until a workplan milestone is checked.

      Labeled by its weakest item. 6 verified, 1 beta.

      Terminal

      claude plugin marketplace add ai-foundry-byu/foundry-marketplace && claude plugin install foundry-guardrails@ai-foundry
      Known limits
      • A seatbelt, not a vault. The hooks match file names and command shapes, so an unusual command such as an archive round trip can still get past them.
      • On smaller models, call a skill by name. Triggering is tuned for Sonnet and Opus.
      What is inside: 6 hooks, 1 skill
      • destructive-guardhookverified
      • secret-guardhookbeta
      • ship-stophookverified
      • stale-write-guardhookverified
      • verify-before-donehookverified
      • worktree-guardhookverified
      • guardrails-helpskillverified

      Source · Item pages

    3. betaStarter set · AI FoundryMIT

      Labeled by its weakest item. 6 verified, 3 beta.

      Terminal

      claude plugin marketplace add ai-foundry-byu/foundry-marketplace && claude plugin install foundry-qa@ai-foundry
      Known limits
      • Signed-in QA needs a test-only sign-in route that is off in production.
      • The full stage 6 check is heavy: each verifier and persona runs its own Chromium.

    9. unratedJDMIT

      claude-bug-squash

      Report a bug and it triages, fixes in an isolated git worktree, proves the bug goes red to green, and gates every fix behind blast-radius caps, a never-touch list and a three-seat review panel.

      Not part of the Foundry's recorded test runs. Its README states its own limits.

      Terminal

      claude plugin marketplace add jddavenportOpen/claude-bug-squash && claude plugin install claude-bug-squash@claude-bug-squash
      Known limits
      • An autonomous merge needs a repro command that fails while the bug is present and passes once it is fixed. Without one, fixes cannot auto-merge.
      • At most one auto-merge a day by default.

      Source

    10. betaJDMIT

      recruit (recruit-copilot)

      Merge the resumes you already have into one experience bank, score open roles against goals you set, tailor a resume per posting, and check that a machine can still read it. It never applies for you.

      Labeled beta in the Foundry marketplace's own recorded runs.

      Terminal

      claude plugin marketplace add jddavenportOpen/recruit-copilot && claude plugin install recruit@recruit-copilot
      Known limits
      • The round-trip check proves the text is present and readable in order. It cannot prove every commercial ATS parses it, so never call it ATS-verified.
      • The built-in PDF reader handles common resume PDFs, not every PDF.

      Source · Write-up

    11. unratedJDMIT

      Clawdacademy (ai-fluency-trainer)

      Scores seven judgment behaviors in your real Claude Code sessions, names your weakest habit and coaches in the flow of work.

      Not part of the Foundry's recorded test runs. Its README states its own limits.

      Its one-line installer runs a script from a third domain. Read the repo's README and install script before you run it.

      Known limits
      • Sync is opt-in and needs a token. Read the data section of the README before you turn it on.

      Source

    Skills

    One folder your agent loads when the task matches.

    1. unratedJDMIT

      contact-list-builder

      Builds a verified list of public business contacts for customer interviews or prospecting. Parallel research lanes, then a script re-downloads every source page to prove each email and phone is there.

      Not part of the Foundry's recorded test runs. Its README states its own limits.

      Terminal

      git clone https://github.com/jddavenportOpen/contact-list-builder ~/.claude/skills/contact-list-builder
      Known limits
      • Public pages only, and guessed emails are never shown as real.
      • Needs Python 3. pdftotext is optional, for contacts that appear only in PDFs.

      Source

    Harnesses and tools

    The machinery around the agents: orgs, fleets, governors, traces.

    1. unratedJDAGPL-3.0 · share changes if you run it as a service

      Clawdling

      Your Claude Code as a whole org: an agent for each project on one map, showing who is working and who needs you, with a receipt when one says done. Local, on your own Claude plan.

      Not part of the Foundry's recorded test runs. Its README states its own limits.

      Paste into Claude Code

      Set up Clawdling for me from https://github.com/jddavenportOpen/clawdling and follow SETUP.md
      Known limits
      • Needs a paid Claude plan (Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise). On Pro, run one or two agents at a time.
      • AGPL-3.0: if you run a modified version as a service, you must share your changes.

      Source · Write-up

    2. unratedJDMIT

      clawd-agent-os

      Tiered Claude agent hierarchies: worktree-isolated fleet spawning, a durable agent bus that never silently returns empty, and one registry for model tiers.

      Not part of the Foundry's recorded test runs. Its README states its own limits.

      Terminal

      git clone https://github.com/jddavenportOpen/clawd-agent-os && cd clawd-agent-os && pip install -e ".[dev]"
      Known limits
      • Needs the Claude Code CLI on your PATH.
      • The durable bus needs a Postgres or Supabase table you provide.

      Source

    3. unratedJDMIT

      warden

      A governor for autonomous agents: autonomy is admitted by how reversible an action is, not by how confident the agent sounds. Zero dependencies.

      Not part of the Foundry's recorded test runs. Its README states its own limits.

      Terminal

      git clone https://github.com/jddavenportOpen/warden && cd warden && pip install -e .
      Known limits
      • It checks that an undo exists, not that the undo works.
      • It governs actions, not prompts. It is not a jailbreak defense.

      Source

    4. unratedJDMIT

      fleetwright

      A self-hosted agent operations OS: a persistent chief of staff that commands a fleet of agents, with a bridge and a web cockpit.

      Not part of the Foundry's recorded test runs. Its README states its own limits.

      Terminal

      git clone https://github.com/jddavenportOpen/fleetwright.git && cd fleetwright && bash scripts/bootstrap.sh
      Known limits
      • The bridge needs access to your own claude CLI.
      • The cockpit is a Node app you run locally.

      Source

    5. unratedJDMIT

      ccstitch

      A local trace store for Claude Code's OpenTelemetry spans that repairs orphaned headless turns and nests child sessions under the tool call that launched them.

      Not part of the Foundry's recorded test runs. Its README states its own limits.

      Terminal

      pipx install git+https://github.com/jddavenportOpen/ccstitch && ccstitch install --dry-run
      Known limits
      • Depends on a Claude Code telemetry beta; span names can change in any release.
      • Single machine, single user, no authentication beyond the local bind.
      • Costs it shows are list-price estimates.

      Source

    6. unratedJDMIT

      harnessview

      Inspect and visualize your agent harness (agents, skills, hooks, MCP servers) and its run history, and spot broken config.

      Not part of the Foundry's recorded test runs. Its README states its own limits.

      Terminal

      git clone https://github.com/jddavenportOpen/harnessview && cd harnessview && npm install && npm run dev
      Known limits
      • Run it from a clone. The README's npx harnessview line does not work yet: the package is not on npm.

      Source · Write-up

    Workflows

    Several of the items above chained into one job, with a check at the end.

    1. Workflow

      0 to 1 product build

      Go from an idea to a shipped app with agents, one stage at a time, with a judge at each gate. Built on foundry-sdlc.

      Read the steps · 2 min

    2. Workflow

      Parallel lanes with worktrees

      Run several coding agents on one repo at once without them overwriting each other. One git worktree per lane, and a guard that keeps each lane in its own tree.

      Read the steps · 2 min

    3. Workflow

      Ship with a done gate

      Never call a feature done until production serves the commit you meant and a browser has walked the user's path on it. Built on foundry-qa.

      Read the steps · 1 min

    4. Workflow

      Bug report to merged fix
